cells.Set by: The Nix lint shell and the Nix `lefthook` wrapper (`flake.nix`).
cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` turns it on. Any other text counts as off. Unset: off. The hook commands try `ci/.venv/bin/ruff` and `ci/.venv/bin/python` first, then the tools on `PATH`.
cells.Effect: With `1`, the Lefthook (Git hook runner) commands `ruff-format`, `ruff-check` and `agent-guidance` run `ruff` and `python3` from `PATH` and do not look in `ci/.venv/bin`. `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` does the same for `python3`. A missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` then fails the hook command. `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix lint shell (`nix develop .#lint`, `x86_64-linux` only) and in the `lefthook` wrapper of the Nix dev shell. `bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh` fails without `1`. Without `1`, a missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` is skipped when `CI` is unset or empty.

cells.Values and default: Text of the form `vvvv:dddd`: a PCI vendor ID of 4 hex digits, a colon, and a device ID of 4 hex digits. The script passes it unquoted to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh`. Unset: `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` gets only the card address. It prints a warning and continues without the ID check.
cells.Effect: Unless its first argument is `unbind`, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks for a device with this vendor and device ID at the card address, then binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space PCI access). A mismatch stops both scripts. The script takes `pci_id` from its environment and never assigns it. It prints the value in each `binding` line. The `unbind` mode does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script. Text in PCI address form replaces the card address.

cells.Values and default: Offset from the base address, as hexadecimal digits without the `0x` prefix. The script adds `0x` in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic without a check. Unset: the offset counts as 0. The first address is the base address `0x37000000000`.
cells.Effect: `bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh` uses `start_address` before it assigns it. On the first pass of its loop it adds the inherited value to the base address `0x37000000000`. It writes a test pattern to that memory address with `./iotools mmio_write64` and reads it back. Each later pass adds the address of the previous pass to the base address again. The script reads the address range of each line of `address_map_1.csv` into `range` and never uses it. It runs `./iotools` from the current directory.

cells.Set by: A developer who runs the tree-vis scripts.
cells.Values and default: A Hugging Face access token. Any non-empty text is used unchanged. Unset: the scripts pass no token, unless an earlier source gives one.
cells.Effect: The tree-vis scripts (they draw token trees for the KV cache documentation) pass the token to `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` when they load a tokenizer. It is the last source. `gen.py` first uses `tokenizer.hf_token` of its YAML input, then `HF_TOKEN`. `tokenizer.py` first uses `--hf-token`, then `HF_TOKEN`. No other file in Tron reads this name.

cells.Set by: CI workflows, as `/tools/uv/<version>/uv`. A developer, to select another `uv`.
cells.Values and default: Command name or path of `uv` (the Python package manager that the repository uses). The text is used as the command. Unset: `make` and the 2 `bin/ci` scripts run `uv` from `PATH`. The Python scripts try `PATH`, then `/tools/uv/uv`. Empty: `make` keeps the empty text.
cells.Effect: `make` runs it for the `*-deps` targets, `python-lock` and the `gen/tokenize_py` build. `ingest/build-model.py` and `bin/extract_logits` run it to start the export scripts of `ingest/export`. CI steps run `$UV sync` to install Python environments, and 2 CI scripts run `bin/ci/benchmark_info.py` with it. Empty value: the `make` recipes have no program name, and the Python and `bin/ci` scripts treat it as unset. With a non-empty `IN_NIX_SHELL`, `make` runs it only for `proxy-test-deps` and `python-lock`. `ingest/build-model.py` does not run it with a non-empty `IN_NIX_SHELL` or with `--export-with-current-python`.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the Gemma 4 tokenizer files. A value that is not an existing directory counts as unset. Unset: the test case uses `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/google/gemma-4-12B-it`. It is skipped when that directory does not exist.
cells.Effect: The Gemma 4 test case of `t_rinzler_tokens` loads its tokenizer from this directory. `t_tokenizers` does not read this variable. It always loads the fixed path `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/google/gemma-4-12B-it`. The test case has the tag `[slow]`. `make test-core`, `make test-host` and `make test-fast` exclude that tag.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the Llama 3.1 tokenizer files. A value that is not an existing directory counts as unset. Unset: the test case uses `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`. It is skipped when that directory does not exist.
cells.Effect: The Llama 3.1 test case of `t_rinzler_tokens` loads its tokenizer from this directory. The test case has the tag `[slow]`. `make test-core`, `make test-host` and `make test-fast` exclude that tag.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the Ministral tokenizer files. A value that is not an existing directory counts as unset. Unset: the test case uses `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512`. It is skipped when that directory does not exist.
cells.Effect: The Ministral test case of `t_rinzler_tokens` loads its tokenizer from this directory. The test case is also skipped when `tokenizer.json`, `chat_template.jinja` or `tokenizer_config.json` is missing in the directory. The test case has the tag `[slow]`. `make test-core`, `make test-host` and `make test-fast` exclude that tag.

cells.Read by: `t_tokenizers`, `t_llguidance`, `t_rinzler_tokens`, Rust unit tests of the `hf_tokenizers_ffi` crate (`t/t_tokenizers.cpp`, `t/t_llguidance.cpp`, `rust/tokenizers/src/lib.rs` and 1 more file)
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory with the Mixtral model files. The C++ tests count a value that is not an existing directory as unset. The Rust tests open `tokenizer.json` in it. Unset: the C++ tests use `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1`, or skip when it is missing. The Rust tests pass and check nothing. Empty: the Rust tests open `/tokenizer.json`.
cells.Effect: Gives the Mixtral tokenizer tests the directory of the model files. It enables 3 Rust unit tests. It replaces the fixed path in 16 test cases of 3 C++ test programs. Rust: when `tokenizer.json` cannot be loaded, 2 tests fail and 1 test prints a skip message. The 16 C++ test cases have the tag `[slow]`. `make test-core`, `make test-host` and `make test-fast` exclude that tag. `t/CMakeLists.txt` does not register the Rust tests.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A value above the maximum is lowered to the maximum. Unset: the test case uses the maximum. Empty: counts as `0`, and the test case skips.
cells.Effect: Sets the largest number of bystander threads (extra waiting threads) that the test case `spin waiter storm at scale (56c cliff)` starts. Smaller rounds with 4, 8, 16 and 32 threads still run when they are not above this number. A result below 8 threads makes the test case skip. The maximum is the number of application CPUs (CPU cores that the process pins its application threads to) minus 3, and at most 53 threads. `0` and negative values cause the skip. The skip message is `Not enough app cpus for a waiter storm`.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `std::stoi`. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoi` throw an exception when the test run starts. Unset: `1`. Empty: `std::stoi` throws an exception when the test run starts.
cells.Effect: A value above `0` multiplies two base counts of the stress test cases of `t_hwalloc`. The counts are the number of threads and the number of operations for each thread. A value of `0` or below changes nothing. The base counts are 1 thread and 30 operations for each thread. Six test cases multiply them by fixed factors. The test case `Extreme contention` starts 32 threads multiplied by the value. The total number of operations grows with the square of the value.

cells.Values and default: `0` or `1`, parsed with `std::stoi`. The test output labels `1` as `C0.1` and `0` as `C0.2`. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoi` throw an exception. Unset: `1`.
cells.Effect: Sets the hint argument of the CPU instruction `tpause` in the spin-wait benchmark (a test loop that polls a flag and does not sleep). The main thread and the worker thread both use it. Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. The test requires a value of at most `1`. The test stores the value in 8 bits before that check. `256` becomes `0` and passes. `-1` becomes `255` and fails.

hints.problem: Rule 8 and 1. Terms with no explanation: "`C0.1`" and "`C0.2`" (two idle states of Intel CPUs), "ledger" in "the ledger code of the CI model cache", "the runner" (a CI machine), "the flake source", "the LSF bridge". In `GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS` the quoted source comment is not marked as a quote.
